data.name: Chandraram
data.gender_notes: Chandraram is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: 1. The name Chandraram is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Chandra' which means 'moon' and 'Ram' which means 'ruler'. 2. In Hindu mythology, Chandraram is considered as a divine name representing the ruler of the moon. 3. It is also believed that the name bestows the blessings of Lord Chandra, the deity of the moon. The name Chandraram carries the meaning “Moon God's Ruler” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Chandraram usually hope their child will grow to embody moon god's ruler and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Represents the divine power of the moon.

vedic_reference.note: This name is derived from the Sanskrit words चंद्रमान (Chandramānaḥ) meaning 'Moon' and राम (Rāmaḥ) meaning 'Protector'. The name Chandraram signifies one who protects the moon.

historical_references.reference:
Chandraram was a renowned Hindu king who ruled over the Vakataka Dynasty from 440 to 460 AD.
Context: Chandraram is best known for his patronage of arts and architecture, as evidenced by the numerous temples and rock-cut caves built during his reign.

Chandraram is also referred to as Chandragupta II in some historical texts. He was a powerful emperor of the Gupta Empire in the late 4th and early 5th centuries AD.
Context: Chandragupta II successfully defended his empire against the invading Hunas and expanded its territory, making it one of the most powerful empires in ancient India.
